title: Big and nef tautological bundles from very ample line bundles on minimal general-type surfaces under the stated numerical and even-exponent conditions
author: Dragos Oprea
source_title: Big and Nef Tautological Vector Bundles over the Hilbert Scheme of Points
difficulty_reason: The proof rewrites the top Segre integral using the established universal generating series and then controls its sign through two nontrivial residue substitutions. In the fully expanded even-exponent case, these substitutions separate a positive range from a vanishing coefficient range, allowing a strict positivity argument after convolution. The surface inequalities then guarantee a positive top self-intersection of the globally generated tautological bundle; simply citing the universal Segre formula would not supply that sign.

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: Select Theorem4.4 with its original hypotheses: X smooth projective minimal surface of general type, k positive, L (k-1)-very ample, chi(L)>=3k and L.K>=2K^2+k+1. Additionally select the explicit Lemma4.1 branch in which m=L.K-2K^2, n=(L-K)^2+3chi(OX)-4k-1 and p=K^2-chi(OX)+3 are all even and n>=0. The complete Claim4.2 residue transformations and its coefficient convolution then supply the new sign core; the three other parity branches whose details are left to the reader are not selected. Full Theorem4.4 numerical reduction, Noether-inequality use and Segre residue substitution4.2 are included. Universal Segre formula4.1 and the established big/nef criterion for a globally generated bundle are author-cited background. No K3, Enriques, blowup or curve variant is separately counted.

statement_scope: Theorem4.4 only with the additional explicit fully expanded branch conditions m,n,p all even and n>=0, where m=L.K-2K^2, n=(L-K)^2+3chi(OX)-4k-1, p=K^2-chi(OX)+3. Original very-ampleness and both numerical inequalities retained. Other parity cases in Lemma4.1 are contextual, not claimed.
editorial_warning: The full printed Lemma4.1 includes three other n>=0 parity cases with details left to the reader. This selected claim is expressly restricted to the expanded all-even branch; no omitted parity proof is supplied or assumed.
